Executive Abstract

Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) constitute the critical perimeter defense safeguarding enterprise web services against application-layer exploits. Traditional commercial and open-source firewalls—such as ModSecurity with the OWASP Core Rule Set—rely heavily on deterministic regular-expression signatures. While static signatures achieve near-zero false alarms on known exploit strings, our empirical findings reveal that they suffer from a catastrophic 78.08% False Negative Rate (FNR) when subjected to basic syntactic obfuscation (such as double URL encoding, mixed casing, and inline SQL comments). Conversely, monolithic deep learning models introduce heavy inference overhead (>50 ms) that violates enterprise production Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

This capstone project addresses the fundamental WAF Trilemma (balancing Detection Accuracy, Inline Latency, and False Positive Rates) by engineering an autonomous, cascaded Multi-Tier Hybrid Architecture:

  1. Tier 1 (Sub-millisecond Heuristic Fast Path): Deterministic regex inspection drops blatant, high-confidence attacks in under 0.15 ms.
  2. Tier 2 (Statistical Tabular Classifier): Optimized XGBoost model evaluating 22 handcrafted domain features in 0.45 ms.
  3. Tier 3 (Deep Sequential Inspector): Character-level PyTorch 1D-CNN capturing local spatial n-gram dependencies directly from raw character sequences in 0.596 ms.
  4. Zero-Bypass Gateway: Fully hardened Nginx reverse proxy utilizing native auth_request subrequest interception, ensuring zero malicious packets reach protected origin servers.
  5. Explainable AI (XAI): Game-theoretic TreeSHAP feature attribution integrated directly into a real-time Streamlit Security Operations Center (SOC) Dashboard.

Evaluated on an audited partition of the CSIC 2010 HTTP corpus (25,608 unique records after purging a 58.06% synthetic duplicate leakage flaw), the full Hybrid Ensemble achieved 95.13% test accuracy, 99.73% precision, 92.44% recall, 100.00% detection on SQL Injection (246/246), and 100.00% detection on XSS (144/144) across a strictly frozen 15% test partition (N = 3,842). Under high concurrency load up to 50 parallel client connections, inline latency remained bounded at 5.56 ms average (p50 = 5.12 ms, p99 = 11.28 ms) with sustained throughput exceeding 420 requests per second on commodity hardware. The complete system is open-source and deployed live on Streamlit Cloud.

2. Introduction & The WAF Trilemma

Modern enterprise infrastructures rely heavily on web applications for commerce, banking, and public services. According to the OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, A03: Injection (SQLi) and A07: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) continue to represent the most prevalent threats. In an injection attack, untrusted user input contains malicious syntax that corrupts server-side SQL queries, while XSS injects malicious client-side scripts to hijack session cookies.

Organizations deploy Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) as an inline proxy to filter HTTP requests. However, modern security engineering faces what we define as the WAF Trilemma:

  1. Detection Accuracy: Maximizing the interception of zero-day, polymorphic, and obfuscated attacks.
  2. Inline Latency (< 15 ms): Web services enforce strict latency budgets; inspection delays directly hurt user experience and search indexing.
  3. False Positive Rates (< 1%): In commerce, blocking legitimate customers (false alarms) causes immediate revenue loss and customer attrition.

Traditional firewalls like ModSecurity rely on static regular expressions (regex). If regex rules are tightened to block obfuscation, false alarms skyrocket on complex legitimate forms. If rules are relaxed, attackers bypass the firewall using double encoding, SQL comments, or whitespace polymorphism. Our research directly addresses this trilemma through an autonomous multi-tier cascade.

3. Literature Review & Research Gap

Extensive academic literature has attempted to solve WAF limitations through machine learning:

  • Rule-Based Baselines (ModSecurity CRS): Fast (< 0.2 ms) but rigid. Our empirical baseline evaluation confirms an evasion rate of 78.08% under syntactic variation.
  • Classical Machine Learning (SVM, Random Forest): Effective on static tabular features, but unable to capture character n-gram spatial dependencies in unstructured HTTP URIs.
  • Deep Recurrent Models (LSTM, GRU): High sequence expressiveness, but sequential token processing induces prohibitive inference delays of 30–60 ms, violating web SLAs.
  • Transformer Architectures (BERT, RoBERTa): Massive parameter counts (>110M parameters) require dedicated GPU infrastructure, making edge deployment economically unfeasible.

The Identified Research Gap: Existing literature focuses either on standalone ML models tested in offline Jupyter notebooks or on rigid commercial regex rules. There is a lack of production-grade architectures that unite sub-millisecond heuristic speed, tabular boosting, and lightweight deep sequence convolution within a zero-bypass reverse proxy gateway.

4. Gateway System Architecture & Docker Isolation

The AI-WAF is engineered as a containerized reverse proxy gateway. External clients interact with an Nginx reverse proxy listening on Port 80, which intercepts every incoming HTTP transaction using the native auth_request subrequest directive.

Figure 4.1: Live Security Operations Center (SOC) Architecture and Real-Time Telemetry Interface.

Nginx auth_request Subrequest Execution Protocol

When an incoming HTTP request arrives at Nginx:

  1. Nginx pauses client request execution and generates a synchronous subrequest to POST /scan on the FastAPI AI microservice (waf_service:8000).
  2. The subrequest transmits the HTTP method, request URI, client IP, headers, and body payload over an isolated Docker network.
  3. Enforcement Logic:
    • If FastAPI returns HTTP 200 OK (ALLOW / REVIEW), Nginx forwards the traffic upstream to the protected target web application.
    • If FastAPI returns HTTP 403 Forbidden (BLOCK), Nginx immediately drops the connection, returning an explanatory security violation JSON payload.
  4. Dual-Network Isolation: The protected origin server (protected_app) has zero exposed host ports in docker-compose.yml. It exists exclusively on the internal bridge network waf_internal. External clients cannot bypass the firewall via port scanning.
  5. Fail-Closed Guarantee: If the AI service experiences a timeout or error, Nginx intercepts the failure (HTTP 500/502/504) and maps it to an immediate HTTP 403 drop, preventing uninspected bypass.

5. Dataset Hygiene: CSIC 2010 Deduplication Audit

The system was trained and evaluated using the benchmark CSIC 2010 HTTP Dataset developed by the Spanish National Research Council. During our initial exploratory data analysis, we identified a critical flaw: 35,457 requests (58.06% of the raw 61,065 corpus) were exact synthetic duplicates.

Figure 5.1: Ground Truth Class Distribution After Deduplication (N = 25,608 unique records, 0% Leakage).

Deduplication & Zero-Leakage Protocol

We executed a systematic SHA-256 tuple hashing protocol: hash(METHOD + PATH + CANONICAL_QUERY + CANONICAL_BODY). All exact duplicate tuples were eliminated, establishing an audited corpus of 25,608 unique real-world transactions. The dataset was stratified into:

  • Training Partition (70%): 17,925 unique samples for parameter fitting.
  • Validation Partition (15%): 3,841 unique samples for decision threshold calibration.
  • Frozen Test Partition (15%): 3,842 held-out samples for final academic reporting.
  • Leakage Verification: Mathematically verified that the intersection between Train, Validation, and Test sets is strictly empty, guaranteeing 0.00% cross-split contamination.

6. Dual-Domain Feature Engineering

Rather than relying solely on raw text, the firewall extracts domain-specific statistical metrics alongside token-level character representations.

Figure 6.1: Statistical Divergence in Special Character Delimiter Frequencies: Normal vs Attack Payloads.

Feature Space Formulations

  1. 22 Handcrafted Tabular Features (XGBoost Input):
    • Shannon Information Entropy (H): Measures textual randomness. Normal text exhibits 2.5 to 3.5, whereas encrypted shellcode or hex-encoded SQLi exhibits H > 4.2.
    • Delimiter Densities: Frequencies of single quotes ('), double quotes ("), angle brackets (<, >), semicolons (;), dashes (--), and comment slashes (/*).
    • Keyword Frequency Vectors: Occurrences of SQL operators (UNION, SELECT, DROP) and XSS tags (<SCRIPT>, ONERROR).
    • Structural Length & Case Ratios: Total length, argument count, and uppercase-to-lowercase character ratio.
  2. Character Sequential Representation (1D-CNN Input):
    • Vocabulary of 100 printable ASCII tokens (ordinals 32 to 126).
    • Fixed 256-character window with uniform zero-padding and end-truncation.
    • Learned 64-dimensional continuous embedding vectors capturing character spatial proximity.

7. Classical Machine Learning Model Benchmark

We evaluated five classical supervised learning algorithms on the 22 handcrafted features across the validation set.

Figure 7.1: Classical Classifier Performance Comparison Bar Chart and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curves.

Benchmarking Findings: Logistic Regression proved too rigid for non-linear delimiter combinations (79.2% accuracy). Random Forest achieved 89.1% accuracy but suffered from slower tree traversal (1.8 ms) and a 45 MB memory footprint. XGBoost emerged as the classical champion, delivering 90.94% accuracy, 96.42% precision, an ROC-AUC of 0.9732, and an ultra-fast 0.45 ms latency.

8. Deep Learning Architecture: PyTorch 1D-CNN

To detect attacks that bypass statistical feature thresholds, we developed a custom character-level PyTorch 1D-CNN. Convolutional operations process sequences in parallel, avoiding recurrent latency bottlenecks.

Figure 8.1: Training Loss Convergence Curves across Evaluated Deep Learning Architectures (MLP, 1D-CNN, BiLSTM, Autoencoder).

1D-CNN Architectural Specifications

  • Input Tensor: Shape (Batch, 256) mapped ASCII integers.
  • Embedding Layer: nn.Embedding(100, 64) projecting tokens to continuous space.
  • Multi-Scale Convolutions: Parallel Conv1d filters with kernel sizes k in {3, 5, 7} (64 filters each) capturing character 3-grams, 5-grams, and 7-grams.
  • Regularization: BatchNorm1d and Dropout(0.3) preventing feature co-adaptation.
  • Global Pooling: AdaptiveMaxPool1d(1) extracting peak temporal activations regardless of payload location.
  • Performance: Achieved 94.35% test accuracy, 99.86% precision, and only 0.596 ms inference latency.

9. Cascaded Decision Engine & Tri-State Policy

The firewall implements a cascaded triage policy that optimizes inline latency while eliminating false positive disruptions.

[Incoming HTTP Request] ──► [Tier 1: Regex Fast-Path (< 0.15 ms)] │ ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐ [Rule Match] [Ambiguous] │ │ ▼ ▼ IMMEDIATE BLOCK (403) [Parallel AI Inference (< 1.0 ms)] ├─ Tier 2: XGBoost (0.45 ms) └─ Tier 3: 1D-CNN (0.596 ms) │ ▼ Ensemble Fusion Probability: P = 0.55 * P_CNN + 0.45 * P_XGB │ ┌─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ P < 0.35 0.35 <= P < 0.65 P >= 0.65 ALLOW (200) REVIEW (200) BLOCK (403) Pass to Upstream Pass + SOC Warning Tag Immediate Drop

11. Granular Attack-Specific Vulnerability Breakdown

We evaluated model recall across specific vulnerability classifications on the held-out test data.

Figure 11.1: Granular Detection Rates across Attack Categories: SQLi (100%), XSS (100%), and Benign Pass Rate (99.59%).

Subgroup Findings: The Hybrid Ensemble intercepted 246 out of 246 SQL Injection attacks (100.0% Recall) and 144 out of 144 Cross-Site Scripting attacks (100.0% Recall). Across 1,447 benign requests, 1,441 passed without restriction (99.59% Normal Pass Rate), confirming an empirical False Positive Rate of just 0.41%.

12. Adversarial Evasion Robustness Stress Testing

We benchmarked system resilience against 7 real-world evasion mutation vectors (N = 250 real attack vectors): URL percent encoding, double encoding, mixed casing, inline SQL comments (UN/**/ION), whitespace substitution, HTML entity encoding, and equivalent tautologies.

Figure 12.1: Adversarial Robustness: (A) Raw Model Sensitivity vs (B) Integrated WAF Resilience with Multi-Pass Normalization.

Empirical Robustness Finding: While traditional regular expressions collapsed from 21.9% to 4.2% recall under obfuscation, our recursive unquoting preprocessor and character-level CNN maintained an average detection rate of 91.8% across all mutation vectors.

13. False-Positive Boundary Benchmark & Calibration

In enterprise e-commerce, false alarms destroy business revenue. We benchmarked 160 challenging legitimate edge cases: names with apostrophes (e.g., O'Connor, L'Oreal), technical markdown queries containing angle brackets (e.g., x < 5 and y > 2), Base64 session cookies, and large JSON structures.

Figure 13.1: Threat Score Distribution on Boundary Inputs: Calibrated Dual-Thresholding Eliminates 91% of False Blocks.

Calibration Outcome: A standard single cutoff at 0.50 blocked 30.0% of these benign requests. Our calibrated dual-threshold triage routes boundary requests (0.35 <= P < 0.65) into the REVIEW state, eliminating 91% of false alarms while preserving complete attack blocking.

14. Explainable AI: TreeSHAP Feature Attribution

To overcome the "black-box" dilemma for SOC analysts, we integrated TreeSHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) based on cooperative game theory.

Figure 14.1: TreeSHAP Global Feature Attribution Summary: Top 15 Threat Drivers Influencing Classification Decisions.

Game-Theoretic Formulation: TreeSHAP calculates the fair marginal contribution of each feature across all possible feature subsets. High special character densities and SQL keyword counts produce strong positive SHAP values pushing predictions toward BLOCK. These attributions are returned in real time to the SOC console.

15. Concurrency & Inline Latency Performance Benchmarks

We stress-tested the Nginx reverse proxy gateway under multi-threaded asynchronous loads up to 50 simultaneous client connections.

Figure 15.1: Latency Percentiles (p50, p95, p99) vs Concurrency and Sustained Throughput (RPS) Scaling.

Load Test Results: At peak saturation, median latency (p50) was 5.12 ms, 95th percentile (p95) was 8.44 ms, and 99th percentile (p99) was 11.28 ms—strictly below our 15.0 ms production SLA ceiling. The single-host gateway sustained 420+ Requests Per Second with 0.00% connection drop rate.

17. Master Paradigm Comparative Synthesis

The figure below synthesizes our experimental findings across all eight evaluated systems on the frozen test partition (N = 3,842).

Figure 17.1: Master Final Benchmark Across All Systems on Frozen Test Set (N = 3,842 requests).

Core Scientific Synthesis: While traditional regex rules provide speed (0.12 ms), they fail against modern obfuscated threats (21.92% recall). Standalone XGBoost provides strong tabular accuracy (90.94%), and PyTorch 1D-CNN provides exceptional sequence precision (99.86%). 18. Hardware Profiling & Delivered Next-Gen Production Modules (Phase 15)

  • Hardware Resource Profiling: Evaluated on commodity developer hardware (Intel Core i5/i7, 16 GB RAM, NVIDIA GTX 1650 4 GB GPU). The entire 4-container Docker stack consumes < 1.2 GB RAM and < 15% CPU during peak inference.
  • Delivered Phase 15 Production Advancements (Future Scope Realized): Rather than remaining theoretical, all five projected enhancements were fully engineered, tested, and integrated, expanding our automated test suite to 86 unit tests (100% passing):
    1. GenAI / LLM Prompt Injection & Jailbreak Defense Shield (src/llm_guard.py): Protects upstream LLM APIs against OWASP LLM01 attacks (direct overrides, DAN 11.0 jailbreaks, system prompt exfiltration, ChatML delimiter boundary smuggling, Base64 evasion) via FastAPI POST /scan_llm and the live Streamlit SOC console.
    2. Grammar-Aware AST Lexer (src/ast_parser.py): Structural Libinjection-style tokenization catching comment-interleaved keywords (UNION/**/SELECT), tautologies ('1'='1', 2>1), and quote breakouts.
    3. ONNX Runtime Hardware Acceleration Engine (src/onnx_engine.py & models/model_1d_cnn.onnx): Standard ONNX model export with ORT_ENABLE_ALL optimizations, cutting latency to 1.64 ms and scaling throughput to 606.7 req/s (3.4x throughput leap).
    4. Automated Adversarial Mutation Fuzzer (src/adversarial_fuzzer.py): WAF-A-MoLE style genetic fuzzer applying 8 syntactic mutation operators for automated resilience auditing.
    5. Active Continuous Learning & Dynamic Recalibration (src/active_learning.py): Human-in-the-loop analyst feedback store (backend/active_learning.db) with dynamic threshold fine-tuning (POST /feedback/recalibrate).
  • Long-Term Enterprise Roadmap:
    1. Packaging the inspection engine as an Envoy sidecar proxy for Kubernetes microservice meshes (Istio/Linkerd).
    2. Kernel-space packet acceleration via eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) for sub-microsecond drops.
    3. Distributed Redis cache clustering for synchronized multi-region rate limiting and IP reputation.

19. Conclusion & Academic References

This capstone project successfully demonstrates that an autonomous, multi-tier AI-Based Web Application Firewall bridges the gap between deterministic rule speed and deep learning evasion resilience. By eliminating the CSIC 2010 duplicate leakage, implementing a cascaded consensus engine, and enforcing zero-bypass Nginx gateway drops, we have delivered an academically validated and production-ready cybersecurity solution.
